parameters: Lichtenhall: white stone and gold leaf, the green spires
of the Morgendom catching the sun, and every afternoon the
roar of the Kaiserarena rolling over the rooftops.
Papers. …A letter under the seal of Asahina? For Her
Imperial Majesty? Hah. Get in line.
Her Majesty receives nobody before the Sonnwende. The
tournament starts in the Kaiserarena, east of the plaza.
After that, maybe. Welcome to Lichtenhall.
The Morgenklinge was given to the Emperor in 313. If it
is anywhere, it's in this city. The Morgendom will know.

parameters.desc: The Empress receives no one before the Sonnwende tournament. The Morgendom (west) might know where the Morgenklinge is.

parameters: desc = The Empress receives no one before the Sonnwende tournament. The Morgendom (west) might know where the Morgenklinge is.
The palace is closed until the Sonnwende. By order.
A statue of a woman in old armor, a sword raised to the
morning. The plinth: SŌRYŪ AKIRA · HELDIN DER MORGENRÖTE
· 312. Around her feet: a crown, a horn, a lantern.
…They gave her a kind face. She didn't have one. She
had a tired face, and she was right about me.
That I would burn the world to kill every demon in it,
if nobody stopped me. Later, Falin.
Imperial steel, Eisenberg rune-steel, and prices to
match. The tournament's good for business.
Elixirs, salts, ether. Everything a hero needs, and
most of what a coward needs too.
The Sonnwende! Eight years Gōki's been champion. Somebody
ought to knock him down. Not me. Somebody.
Her Majesty's new lady-in-waiting, Lady Tsumugi, did you
see her? Such a lovely laugh. Such long fingers.
People go missing in the lower city. The watch says they
went to the Wall. Nobody goes to the Wall.
The Morgendom's bells ring the hours. They stop ringing,
we're all in trouble, my grandfather said.
Are you a hero? You look like a hero. Sort of.
